doc.name: A — fine jewelry catalogue, hands in frame, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: pavé diamond eternity band
Category: fine jewelry
Shot programme: hands in frame
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium fine jewelry product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-hand scale in a hands in frame treatment.

SUBJECT. A pavé diamond eternity band. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Held in a hand that provides scale, hand cropped at the wrist. Shoot on a 40mm normal at f/22, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against wet terrazzo, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a desaturated Nordic palette with cold blue shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
